data.narrative:
DigiChem is a Seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Greg Ellson and Ben Berman, having raised $4M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a universe of 9 private peers and 1 public comparable in the Robotics & Manufacturing sector, including companies such as Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, and Locus Robotics.

A peer-median approach was not applicable due to insufficient comparable datapoints—while 10 same-sector peers exist, only 1 operates at the same stage, and none met the threshold of 3+ comparables in adjacent stage buckets or similar valuation tiers needed for reliable median extraction. Consequently, analysis relied on stage-progression methodology, applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical for Seed-to-next-stage advancement to the $4M raised proxy, yielding an implied valuation of $10M.

The triangulated valuation range supported by this analysis is $8M to $12M, with a median point of $10M. The narrow methodological base—derived from a single applicable approach—represents the primary uncertainty. Validation would benefit from either expanding the peer set within Robotics & Manufacturing to achieve sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables, or from additional transaction data for similar-tier private companies. Revenue trajectory, technology defensibility, and market traction remain critical valuation drivers not quantified in this analysis.
